title: Deep learning detects and grades neonatal intraventricular haemorrhage on ultrasound
summary: A deep learning model with a convolutional block attention module was developed on 773 participants from two hospitals and tested prospectively on 287 participants. Retrospective AUC was 0.99 (precision 0.92, recall 0.93), and prospective two-centre AUC was 0.961 with accuracy 0.89. The authors suggest value for primary and community hospitals.
ai_technology: Deep learning model with convolutional block attention module on cranial ultrasound

evidence.tested: Retrospective development (n=773) and prospective two-centre validation (n=287).
evidence.unknown: Preterm and healthy infants at two hospitals only; clinical outcome impact not assessed; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning detects and grades haemorrhage in cranial ultrasound images.
